# SEO-282: Give each section a stable fragment identifier

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | `ai-retrieval` |

| Change safety | `REVIEW_REQUIRED` |
| Evidence tier | `A` |
| Confidence | `MEDIUM` |

## Statement

Every heading that introduces a distinct section carries an identifier that survives edits to the heading text, so a link to that passage keeps resolving after the wording changes.

## Rationale

An identifier derived from the heading text breaks whenever the heading is reworded, which silently invalidates every link anyone made to that section.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "content_publication",
    "public_documents"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Assign the identifier once and keep it, rather than regenerating it from the current heading on each build. Where an identifier must change, leave the previous one in place as an additional target.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Collect section identifiers per route across two builds and report any that changed while the section itself persisted.
- Evidence: `RENDERED_HTML`, `BUILD_OUTPUT`, `ROUTE`
- Automated check: none.

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `AI_ASSISTANT_RETRIEVAL`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: The cited specification defines how a fragment resolves to an element, which is the mechanism this record depends on. No retrieval system documents using fragments to cite a passage, so the benefit claimed here is that existing links keep working, not that a passage becomes more citable.
